neighbours.label: the imperative verb (or its 'with' complement) that gives the reader a practical health, safety or home tip (Use…, choose…, eat…, brush… with), versus the same verbs narrating what someone did
fire:
Ways to save water at home:
- Use a bucket instead of a hose to wash the car.
If you burn your hand, hold it under cool running water and use a clean bandage.
When shopping for bulbs, choose LED lights that last for years.
To keep your heart healthy, eat more vegetables and less salt.
Before a long hike, use insect spray on your arms and legs.
Wash your hands often with warm water and soap during flu season.
To stay warm in winter, choose wool socks over cotton ones.
For better sleep, use heavy curtains to keep the bedroom dark.
quiet: Last summer my neighbour used a bucket instead of a hose to wash the car.
When she burned her hand, the nurse ran cool water over it and applied a clean bandage.
The hotel chain chose LED lights for all of its rooms last year.
My grandfather ate vegetables from his garden every day of his life.
On the long hike, Tom sprayed insect repellent on his arms and legs.
The surgeon washed her hands with warm water and soap before the operation.
In the old story, the miller wore wool socks all winter.
The new tenants hung heavy curtains in the bedroom last week.

predictions: advice imperatives 0.4+; the same actions narrated in past or third person near 0
short: imperative verb of a practical tip
